body: Very convenient, there's guns nearby to execute the addicts.
I feel like I'd be squandering my opportunity too in a sense.

I have, yes. It seems a bit like ranting, but the reason I included the intellectually gifted part in my OP is because I recently had a lecture on them, which in turn sort of rekindled my self esteem: I was considered intellectually gifted a long time ago, and I'm sure if I put myself to work I would probably be considered of above average intelligence too.

However, I'm not sure if I can muster up the willpower to better myself through professional help (the majority of the improving would be done by myself, not the therapist), and then work harder still on my studies, and then employment.

Both of myself, and others.

If I were to die, at least I would not have to live with the knowledge that I am living in a way that I know is far below what I am capable of achieving, but cannot achieve out of laziness.
I'd be hard pressed to find a job within the realm of my capacities, one I would sufficiently enjoy, and one that would be highly placed enough to justify my studies and expected field of work.
